notes: supply-requisition-queue's assertion set was too weak to differentiate the configs — both hit 5/5 despite without_skill producing no prototype and no synthesis file. The real gap in that eval only shows up qualitatively; the next iteration should add assertions for prototype production and explicit numeric confidence.

The with_skill runs consistently take roughly 2x the time and ~25% more tokens than baseline. That's the expected cost of the extra phases (confirm-the-ask, synthesis file, confidence scoring, simulated feedback rounds, prototype build) — worth stating plainly to the user as a tradeoff, not hiding it.

The two evals with meaningful, well-specified assertions (console-ux-stakeholder-brief and dispatch-acceptance-drop-cold) show a real and consistent gap: without_skill fails exactly the assertions that reward structural discipline (ask-vs-answer separation, numeric confidence, specific ticket-vs-data contradiction naming, guaranteed prototype production) rather than raw content quality, which both configs handle reasonably well on their own.

Baselines performed better than a from-scratch agent typically would, most likely because this repo's own CLAUDE.md already instructs fact/hypothesis/conclusion separation and source citation — the skill's lift here is probably underestimated relative to a context with no such project instructions.
